classification.difficultyReason: Use the scaffolded parts to differentiate displacement, solve for zero velocity, compare stationary and endpoint values, and interpret absolute displacement and greatest velocity.

content.prompt: The displacement of a particle from the origin is given by $x(t)=2t^3-6t^2-30t$, where $x$ is metres from the origin and $t$ is time in seconds, $0\le t\le3.5$. Give rounded numerical answers to 2 decimal places where needed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the velocity and acceleration at any time $t$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=6t^2-12t-30\\a(t)&=\frac{dv}{dt}\\&=12t-12\end{align*}$$Velocity is in metres per second and acceleration is in metres per second squared.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the initial velocity and acceleration.

children.label: c
children.prompt: At what time is the velocity zero?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}6t^2-12t-30&=0\\t^2-2t-5&=0\\t&=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{24}}{2}\\&=1\pm\sqrt6\end{align*}$$Only $1+\sqrt6$ lies in $0\le t\le3.5$, so the velocity is zero at $t=1+\sqrt6\text{ s}\approx3.45\text{ s}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the furthest the particle travels from the origin?

answer.worked: Compare displacement at the stationary time and the domain endpoints: $$\begin{align*}x(0)&=0\\x(3.5)&=2(3.5)^3-6(3.5)^2-30(3.5)\\&=-92.75\\x(1+\sqrt6)&=-34-24\sqrt6\\&\approx-92.79\end{align*}$$The global maximum displacement is $0$ and the global minimum is $-34-24\sqrt6$ metres. Distance from the origin is $|x(t)|$, so the furthest distance is $34+24\sqrt6\text{ m}\approx92.79\text{ m}$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: During what time interval is the velocity negative?

answer.worked: $$v(t)=6(t^2-2t-5).$$The velocity–time parabola opens upwards and has roots $t=1-\sqrt6$ and $t=1+\sqrt6$. Therefore $v(t)<0$ between these roots. Since $1-\sqrt6<0$, restricting to the given domain gives $$0\le t<1+\sqrt6.$$The upper boundary is approximately $3.45$ seconds.

children.label: f
children.prompt: When is the velocity greatest in this domain? (Hint: compare the velocity at stationary points and the domain endpoints.) What was the velocity at the time, and what is the significance of this point graphically?

answer.short: At $t=3.5\text{ s}$, the greatest velocity is $1.5\text{ m/s}$. This is the global maximum at the right endpoint of the velocity–time graph; the displacement–time graph has its greatest gradient there.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\frac{dv}{dt}&=12t-12\\12t-12&=0\\t&=1\end{align*}$$Since $\frac{d^2v}{dt^2}=12>0$, this stationary point is a minimum of velocity. Compare the stationary and endpoint values: $$\begin{align*}v(0)&=-30\text{ m/s}\\v(1)&=6-12-30\\&=-36\text{ m/s}\\v(3.5)&=6(3.5)^2-12(3.5)-30\\&=1.5\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$$The greatest velocity is $1.5\text{ m/s}$ at $t=3.5\text{ s}$. Graphically, this is the global maximum at the right endpoint of the velocity–time graph. The displacement–time graph has its greatest gradient in the domain at this time.
